risk_if_not_implemented: Without Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC) Supply Chain Flow-Down Requirements, cryptographic protections may be inadequate or quantum-vulnerable, risking future decryption of currently protected data.

compensating_control_1.name: Supply Chain Risk Management (SCRM)
compensating_control_1.description:
Mechanisms exist to:
(1) Evaluate security risks and threats associated with Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) supply chains; and
(2) Take appropriate remediation actions to minimize the organization's exposure to those risks and threats, as necessary.
compensating_control_1.justification: Supply Chain Risk Management (SCRM) (TPM-03) provides risk identification and prioritization that compensates for the absence of Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC) Supply Chain Flow-Down Requirements (QTS-03.4) by enabling informed decisions about where to focus resources to manage residual exposure. Given the process-oriented nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.

compensating_control_2.name: Third-Party Contract Requirements
compensating_control_2.description: Mechanisms exist to require contractual requirements for applicable security, compliance and resilience requirements with third-parties, reflecting the organization's needs to protect its Technology Assets, Applications, Services and/or Data (TAASD).
compensating_control_2.justification: Third-Party Contract Requirements (TPM-05) provides third-party oversight and contractual controls that compensates for the absence of Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC) Supply Chain Flow-Down Requirements (QTS-03.4) by extending security obligations and monitoring third-party risk in lieu of direct primary control implementation. Given the process-oriented nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.
